Built on the principle of **"feeling over features"**, LÜQ is not a standard chatbot. It does not argue, converse, or offer solutions. It simply reads the emotional tone of the user's input and attempts to make them feel understood.

custom.title: Dizzaract Digital Twin Workflow & Week-Wise Timeline
custom.content:
[FAR LABS / DIZZARACT DIGITAL TWIN — FULL CONTRACT & ARCHITECTURE CONTEXT]
Engagement: 45-day freelance contract with UAE-based FAR Labs (Dizzaract studio) for their Unreal Engine 5 FPS game, Farcana. Shailesh delivered and shipped the complete project in 33 days (12 days ahead of schedule).
Team: Shailesh + teammate Honey, working under the supervision of FAR Labs' Lead AI Engineer (Abdulla Shafeeg / Tanmay Bisen). Shailesh owned model architecture, training loops, RL reward formulation, and ONNX/TensorRT optimization; Honey assisted with data preprocessing and evaluation clips.

=== 5-WEEK TIMELINE & DELIVERABLES (COMPLETED IN 33 DAYS) ===
- Week 1 (Days 1-5): Telemetry Pipeline & Calibration JSONs
  Downloaded 30Hz match telemetry from AWS S3. Cleaned and normalized data with pandas. Built feature extraction pipeline using scipy to generate per-player calibration JSONs: reaction time distribution (mean 250ms, sigma 40ms), aim variance (pitch/yaw sigma, jitter Hz), spray deviation per shot with recovery rate, movement smoothness via FFT, and decision hesitation (mean 310ms).
- Week 2 (Days 6-10): Inverse Dynamics Model (IDM) & Dataset Expansion
  Only 50 matches had complete button-press labels; 500+ hours of match replays had only screen observations. Built a non-causal IDM that looks at frame (t-1) and frame (t+1) to predict action (t). Trained on the 50 labeled matches, then pseudo-labeled all 500+ hours of replays — expanding the usable training dataset by 8x.
- Week 2-3 (Days 11-17): Behavioral Cloning Sub-Models
  Designed and trained 4 specialized sub-models in PyTorch using supervised Behavioral Cloning:
  1. Tactical Brain: Lightweight MLP (128 -> 64) running at 2Hz (every 15 ticks) for macro decisions (push, retreat, flank, hold, heal) using Cross-Entropy loss.
  2. Movement Model: 4-layer Seq2Seq Transformer with a 90-tick history window for directional movement, stance, and jump/sprint using MSE + BCE loss.
  3. Aim Model: 2-layer LSTM with temporal attention for tracking and flick shots, conditioned on spray_deviation and recovery_rate from the calibration JSON using MSE + BCE loss.
  4. Weapon Selector: 6-way classification MLP (64 -> 32 -> 6) using Cross-Entropy loss.
  Why BC first: If RL runs first, the bot finds its own mathematical optimal strategy and human style is wiped out. BC locks the agent inside the real player's behavioral envelope first.
- Week 3-4 (Days 18-26): Headless UE5 Gym Bridge & PPO Fine-Tuning
  Wired a Gym-compatible interface (reset/step) to a headless Unreal Engine 5 build via shared memory, running 8 parallel instances (VecEnv) for high-throughput training. Ran PPO (Proximal Policy Optimization) self-play fine-tuning with a custom style-preserving reward formula:
  Reward = alpha * Combat (kills, damage, survival) + beta * Objectives - lambda * KL(agent || player)
  Lambda annealing: Lambda started high (5.0) to strictly enforce the player's style, then annealed down to 1.0 over 2,000 episodes so combat performance could improve within that style boundary. Gaussian KL on continuous actions, categorical KL on discrete actions. Added an action tempo penalty via autocorrelation to match the player's decision rhythm (100ms twitchy vs 400ms+ patient). Also trained the learned Fusion Gating Network to resolve sub-model conflicts (e.g. Tactical says retreat while Movement wants to push).
- Week 4-5 (Days 27-33): ONNX Export, TensorRT Optimization & Discriminator Evaluation
  Exported all 5 models to ONNX. PyTorch raw inference was 60-80ms (way too slow for a 30Hz game). Applied NVIDIA TensorRT optimizations: INT8 quantization on Movement Transformer and Weapon MLP, FP16 on Aim LSTM (aim precision is too style-critical for INT8). Implemented IO Binding to keep observation and action tensors permanently in GPU memory, and ran Tactical and Weapon models in parallel with CUDA streams. Result: Total stack latency dropped to 12.3ms on an NVIDIA A100 GPU (beating the strict 15ms budget).
  Evaluation: Built a style discriminator (learned Turing test classifier). Evaluated on 100 real player clips vs 100 bot clips. Discriminator accuracy dropped to 57.8% (barely above a 50% coin flip), proving the bot was nearly indistinguishable from the human player.
  Shipped all 5 ONNX models, calibration JSONs, and documentation on Day 33 of the 45-day contract.

=== TENSOR SPECIFICATIONS ===
- Observation Tensor: float[256] at 30Hz (player coordinates X/Y/Z, health, ammo, enemy positions in FOV, score, game state).
- Action Tensor: float[32] mixed output:
  - 5 Continuous: indices 0-1 (move forward/strafe), 5-6 (aim pitch/yaw deltas), 14 (grenade yaw offset).
  - 11 Binary @ 0.5 threshold: jump, sprint, ADS, fire, reload, melee, grenade, ability_1/2, use_item, interact.
  - 2 Ordinal: index 2 stance (Stand/Crouch/Prone), index 10 fire_mode (Single/Burst/Auto).
  - 6 Softmax Argmax: indices 15-20 weapon slots (1-6).
  - 7 Auxiliary / Informational: index 8 aim_target_lock, 21-25 tactical weights, 30-31 reserved.

About the Role:
We're looking for a highly motivated AI Product Engineer who loves building innovative AI products from the ground up. This role is for someone who constantly explores the latest AI models, frameworks, and tools, rapidly prototypes new ideas, and turns them into production-ready applications. You should be comfortable working independently, making technical decisions, and delivering high-quality AI solutions that create measurable business impact.

Responsibilities:
• Design, build, and deploy AI-powered products from concept to production.
• Research and evaluate the latest AI models, frameworks, and emerging technologies.
• Develop AI applications using LLMs, AI agents, RAG pipelines, multimodal models, and modern automation tools.
• Rapidly prototype new product ideas and validate them through experimentation.
• Design scalable software architectures for AI applications.
• Build backend services, APIs, and integrations to support AI products.
• Work independently to solve complex technical challenges with minimal supervision.
• Continuously improve products through testing, iteration, and performance optimization.
• Share knowledge and recommend new technologies that can create competitive advantages for the company.

Requirements:
• Hands-on experience building applications using modern AI models and frameworks.
• Deep understanding of LLMs, AI agents, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), automation, and multimodal AI.
• Ability to independently design, build, test, and deploy products.
• Strong software engineering skills using Python and JavaScript/TypeScript.
• Experience building APIs and working with cloud services.
• Strong understanding of software architecture and scalable system design.
• Excellent problem-solving skills with a strong bias toward execution.
• Self-driven mindset with outstanding research and continuous learning abilities.

Nice to Have:
• Experience with vector databases, embedding pipelines and AI orchestration frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph, or similar.
• Familiarity with Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD, and cloud deployment.
• Knowledge of frontend frameworks such as React or Next.js.
• Familiarity with PHP programming.
